Users of the latest version of Claude Code on macOS and Linux can now send messages between sessions to share findings, ask questions, and coordinate work. Details below.

Claude Code Adds Cross-Session Messaging

Anthropic recently announced a new feature that should prove very useful for users who frequently run multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code version v2.1.224, different sessions can send messages to each other, sharing updates and other relevant information. This feature is especially useful when users have multiple sessions handling different parts of the same project at the same time.

Below is the documentation released by Anthropic regarding this new feature:

Anthropic stated that the best use cases for this new feature include: handing off work, coordinating parallel worktrees, checking on the status of long-running processes, and replying to messages across machines.

The company added that users do not need to bother composing the message content themselves. The user's prompt only needs to contain what they wish to convey, and Claude will write the actual message on their behalf.

It is worth noting that the cross-session messaging feature does not apply to approving permission requests or changing settings. Commands such as /compact will be sent as plain text rather than being executed as actual commands; and if handling the message requires permissions, the receiving party will still request approval from the user.
